findings.evidence: Roadmap `TauCetiRoadmap/IntegralLattices/README.md` Layer 2: "For a carrier basis, use the dual basis and Smith normal form to give `A_L ≃ ∏ i, ZMod dᵢ` ... Relate these factors to the Smith normal form of the Gram matrix"; Layer 1: "For every carrier basis, define the integral Gram matrix"; `Suggested.lean:160` `gramMatrix {ι} [Fintype ι] (e : Basis ι ℤ L.carrier)`. `Basic.lean:186` `ofBasis` carrier is `span ℤ (range b)` for the user's `b`, not `chooseBasis`.
findings.fix: Parameterize on `{ι} [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι ℤ L.carrier)`: `L.dualCarrier = span ℤ (range (L.form.dualBasis _ (b.extendOfIsLattice ℚ)))`, `dualBasisElem b i`, `dualCarrierBasis b : Basis ι ℤ L.dualCarrier` with `dualPairingEquiv (dualCarrierBasis b i) = b.dualBasis i`. The `chooseBasis` instances are then the specialization at `b := Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ L`; the proofs are unchanged.
findings.issue: The whole dual-basis API is fixed to `Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ L` (via `L.rationalBasis`): `dualCarrier_eq_span_dualBasis` (173), `dualBasisElem` (231), `coe_dualBasisElem` (240), `dualPairingEquiv_dualBasisElem` (249), `dualCarrierBasis` (269), `dualCarrierBasis_apply` (276). A user holding a lattice from `ofBasis`/`ofGramMatrix` cannot relate its own basis to a dual basis; `chooseBasis` is an unrelated opaque basis.

findings.evidence: Lines 68-78 use only `Basis.extendOfIsLattice_apply` and `b.span_eq`; `Module.Basis.extendOfIsLattice` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean:138) takes an arbitrary `b : Basis κ R M` with no finiteness or freeness constraint.
findings.fix: State `theorem span_range_extendOfIsLattice {κ} {N : Submodule ℤ V} [N.IsLattice ℚ] (b : Basis κ ℤ N) : Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (b.extendOfIsLattice ℚ)) = N` with the same proof.
findings.issue: `span_range_extendOfIsLattice` is stated only for `Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ N`, although its proof uses nothing about that basis; this forces the `funext` detour in `span_range_rationalBasis` (166-169) and blocks the arbitrary-basis version of the lemmas above.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:105 `congr_arg Cardinal.toNat (Submodule.IsLattice.rank' ℚ L.carrier)` vs Dual.lean:192 `congr_arg Cardinal.toNat (Submodule.IsLattice.rank' ℚ L.dualCarrier)`; Mathlib provides `IsLattice.rank'` for arbitrary lattices but only `finrank_of_pi` at finrank level.
findings.fix: Prove `theorem finrank_of_isLattice (N : Submodule ℤ V) [N.IsLattice ℚ] : Module.finrank ℤ N = Module.finrank ℚ V := congr_arg Cardinal.toNat (Submodule.IsLattice.rank' ℚ N)` once (next to the other general lemmas) and derive `finrank_carrier` and `finrank_dualCarrier` from it.
findings.issue: `finrank_dualCarrier` repeats the proof term of `finrank_carrier` (Basic.lean:103-105) verbatim for a second special case; both are instances of a statement about any full submodule.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean:27-28 sets `[CommRing R] [Field S] [Algebra R S]`; `dualSubmoduleToDual_injective` (line 82) and `dualSubmodule_flip_dualSubmodule_of_basis` (line 126) hold at that level, and line 67 records the TODO "Show that this is perfect when `N` is a lattice and `B` is nondegenerate" — the roadmap asks to "Complete its advertised missing lattice/perfect-pairing consequences" (README.md:105-108).
findings.fix: State them over `{R K V}` with `[CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] [Module.IsTorsionFree R K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] [Module K V] [IsScalarTower R K V]` — the hypotheses of `Submodule.IsLattice.free`. The proofs carry over: replace `FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective ℤ ℚ` by the same lemma at `R K` and `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul ℚ` by `algebraMap_smul`.
findings.issue: `dualSubmoduleToDual_surjective` (82), `dualSubmoduleEquivDual` (116), `dualSubmodule_dualSubmodule_flip` (124) and `dualSubmodule_flip_dualSubmodule` (138) are general submodule results — they mention neither `IntegralLattice` nor anything ℚ-specific — but are pinned to ℤ ⊆ ℚ, one level below the Mathlib API they complete, whose injectivity companion is proved for general `R`/`S`.

summary: The dual-basis API and the general span lemma are hardcoded to `Module.Free.chooseBasis` instead of an arbitrary carrier basis, which the roadmap's next targets (Gram matrix, Smith normal form, `ofGramMatrix`) require; `finrank_dualCarrier` duplicates `finrank_carrier`'s proof for a special case of a one-line general lemma. The five general submodule results are also stated only for ℤ ⊆ ℚ though Mathlib's surrounding API is at general `R`/`K`.
